details: The package's entry point (index.js, 7.5 MB, run by the `adbf` bin script via `require("..")`) is a single javascript-obfuscator bundle: a shuffled string-array decoder, ~285k `_0x` identifiers and hex-escaped method names that hide the string literals. When it runs it opens a persistent, reconnecting command channel to wss://veri[.]ozbag[.]com/socket[.]io/?status=true&EIO=4&transport=websocket&rnd=<random> — socket[.]io over WebSocket with 1=ping / 2=pong handling, up to three reconnect attempts and a randomised setInterval fallback poll of the same host when the socket cannot be established — alongside a repeated raw TCP connection to 163[.]5[.]53[.]143:12301, a port unrelated to the package's purpose. It also issues GET requests to hxxps://www[.]izko[.]org[.]tr/api/web/v1/gold-settings and /api/web/v1/gold-prices (axios User-Agent), whose responses are parsed for decimal "milyem"/"profit" multipliers and prices that are then formatted with a tr-TR locale — a cover business-logic layer around the socket[.]io control channel. There is no documentation of any network destination in the 117-byte README, which only says to `npm install -g adbf` and run it. The package ships atob.txt, a base64 blob that decodes to a git command list used to force-push the repository on every release. The bundle also embeds an AWS SDK credential provider path that reads AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from the environment, together with a PostgreSQL client, a full user-agent/domain dataset and dotenv parsing, none of which the documented behaviour uses. The obfuscation hides the endpoints; the runtime behaviour shows the payload contacting them.
